prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The official rate limits for the GitHub REST API depend on whether the request is authenticated or not. For unauthenticated requests, the limit is based on the originating IP address. For authenticated requests using a personal access token (Classic) or OAuth App, the limit is tied to the user account. Note that GitHub Enterprise Server and GraphQL API may have different limits, but the standard REST API v3 limits are as follows.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests using Basic Authentication, OAuth, or personal access tokens (classic), you can make up to 5,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests via Personal Access Tokens (classic), OAuth, or Basic Auth are limited to 5,000 requests per hour.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For unauthenticated requests, the rate limit allows you to make up to 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour.
